props.title: Easy Riders, Raging Bulls: How the Sex 'n' Drugs 'n' Rock 'n' Roll Generation Saved Hollywood

sections.content: The revolutionary New Hollywood era exploded in the late 1960s when maverick filmmakers like Dennis Hopper and Peter Fonda created Easy Rider (1969), a countercultural phenomenon that proved young directors could deliver both artistic vision and box office success. This documentary, based on Peter Biskind's landmark book, captures the raw energy and creative freedom of that era through candid interviews with the key players. We see how Francis Ford Coppola leveraged the success of The Godfather (1972) to build his own studio, while Martin Scorsese emerged from the New York underground with Mean Streets (1973) and William Friedkin shocked audiences with The Exorcist (1973).

movies.title: Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker's Apocalypse
movies.slug: Documentary chronicling the chaotic making of Apocalypse Now. Essential companion piece.

sections.content: The documentary reveals how personal demons and unchecked ambition led to both masterpieces and disasters. After Heaven's Gate (1980) became one of the biggest flops in history, the era of director-driven films effectively ended. But the legacy of New Hollywood innovations remains massive - from Taxi Driver (1976) to Apocalypse Now (1979), these filmmakers pushed boundaries in style, content and production methods. The film doesn't shy away from the dark side, showing how cocaine, ego and studio pressure destroyed careers and relationships.

Through archival footage and revealing interviews, we see the full arc of the movement - from the early triumphs of The Graduate (1967) and Bonnie and Clyde (1967) through the blockbuster success of Jaws (1975) and Star Wars (1977), which ironically helped end the era of personal filmmaking they championed. The documentary captures both the exhilarating creative freedom and the self-destructive excess that defined this pivotal period. SUBHEAD: The Legacy of New Hollywood

movies.title: Heaven's Gate
movies.slug: Michael Cimino's ambitious Western that bankrupted United Artists and ended the New Hollywood era.

sections.content: While the era ended, its influence shaped the next generation of filmmakers. Directors like Quentin Tarantino, Paul Thomas Anderson and David Fincher were directly inspired by New Hollywood's bold storytelling and technical innovations. The documentary shows how films like Five Easy Pieces (1970) and The Last Detail (1973) created a new language of American cinema that still resonates today. Even as the industry shifted back to more commercial fare, the artistic ambition of New Hollywood permanently altered what was possible in mainstream filmmaking.
